Reactome:R-MTU-936654.description: The CysM-CysO route in Mycobacterium tuberculosis transfers O-phosphoserine onto thiocarboxylated CysO, then Mec releases L-cysteine and regenerates the carrier. The graph begins at CysO-COSH: the upstream MoeZ sulfur-charging step is excluded because its physiological sulfur donor is unresolved. Carrier modification states, PLP-bearing CysM and the source zinc-containing, cleaved Mec assembly remain distinct.

exclude_reactions.Reactome:R-MTU-936590: Excluded placeholder chemistry: the source admits the sulfur donor is unknown, despite drawing free sulfide as a substrate (Reactome reaction comment; PMID16104727). This does not reject MoeZ involvement.

Reactome:R-MTU-936721.description: The Mycobacterium tuberculosis O-acetylserine route joins CysH/Sir sulfate reduction with CysE serine acetylation and CysK1-dependent cysteine synthesis. The outdated CysK2 O-acetylserine reaction is excluded: CysK2 uses a distinct O-phosphoserine route. Native thioredoxin and ferredoxin states and PLP-bearing CysK1 are retained. Reactome chemical forms include sulfurous acid, sulfide(2-) and acetic acid; this graph does not claim physiological protonation or complete stoichiometric balance.

exclude_reactions.Reactome:R-MTU-936745: Excluded contradictory OAS substrate assignment: direct experiments show CysK2 does not react with OAS (PMID25022854); its OPS/thiosulfate route is distinct from both this route and CysM-CysO.

Reactome:R-MTU-936635.description: Mycobacterium tuberculosis sulfate uptake and activation links SubI binding, CysTWA transport, CysD/CysNC-dependent APS synthesis, APS phosphorylation and the CysQ PAPS-hydrolysis branch. GTP hydrolysis is coupled to APS synthesis, correcting its placement on APS kinase in Reactome. This record does not assert exclusive sulfate dependence, universal enzyme essentiality or complete stoichiometric balance. CysQ PAPS activity is qualitatively supported; PAP is its better-characterized substrate.
